Filed by the director seat, summon #25 (`session_012GcsUbuqFGBibkEDMRC1eE`), executing ruling batch #192 item 5 letter B (objectstack#19186, maintainer 「192 同意」). ⛔ Filed bare: `domain:*`, `priority:*` and `type` are triage's production. objectstack#19186 carries `Blocked-by:` on this card — the spec half (declaring the key on the three record blocks) waits for this fix to be installable.

## The defect, as measured by the #18159 dev (PR objectstack#19185's `os-dev-report`) — ⛔ re-derive before acting

`record:quick_actions.requiredPermissions` is published in `@objectstack/spec` as `z.array(z.string())` with the describe 「Hide the whole bar unless the current user holds every named permission on this object」. The renderer evaluates each name through `perms.can(objectName, name)`, whose second argument is the closed `PermissionActionSchema` enum (create/read/update/delete/execute/manage/configure/share/export/import/admin) — ⛔ not the ADR-0066 capability set the same word means on `action` / `app` / `field` / `bulkAction`.

- `MePermissionsProvider`: an unmapped name falls back to the object's `allowRead` bit. Measured with an empty `systemPermissions`: `crm.manage` → `true`, `manage` → `true`, `admin` → `true` — **a capability nobody holds passes for every reader of the object**.
- Role-based `PermissionProvider`: the same name is refused for everyone when the object carries a permission config and allowed for everyone when it does not.
- ⇒ the two stock providers contradict each other and neither consults the caller's capability set. The published describe is false under a stock provider; the failure is silent (no refusal, no warning, no log).

⚠️ These readings were taken by the #18159 dev and relayed by the filing seat of objectstack#19186; the director seat did not re-run them. Step 1 of this card is to reproduce them with a lit control.

## Ruling this card executes

`requiredPermissions` on a record block is an **ADR-0066 capability set**, one meaning across every UI surface. `record:quick_actions.requiredPermissions` is evaluated through the capability path (`hasCapabilities` / `systemPermissions`), **fail-closed**: an unheld **or unknown** capability hides the whole bar. ⛔ `can()`'s semantics are untouched — no other caller moves. Precedent: the app-shell CHANGELOG entry that fixed a bare name to mean an ADR-0066 system capability.

## Acceptance

- Pins on both stock providers: with `requiredPermissions: ['crm.manage']` and an empty capability set the bar is **hidden**; with the capability held it renders; an unknown name hides; an empty array renders (no gate). One control asserting `can()` answers exactly what it answered before for an object action.
- The reading path is the capability set, ⛔ not `perms.can()` with a capability name.
- No new key, no spec change in this repo; `Clause-②` declared from the diff (a runtime behaviour change behind a published key ⇒ expected `no`); changeset per the package's convention.

## Sequencing

Lands first. objectstack#19186 (the spec half: the same key with the same describe on the three record blocks) unblocks when this fix is **installable** by spec's consumers, ⛔ not merely merged. objectstack#18159's third key stays out of PR objectstack#19185 until then.
